coverage: Eligibility sequences in the purposive corpus. Axes have different count ranges. The title sequence excludes titles that fail the English-likely gate or lack an uploader attribution. The caption sequence removes two unavailable tracks, three non-English tracks, one additional concordance sample, five videos without eligible matched titles, and three singleton publisher records. The final matched matrix therefore uses22videos from11publishers; the larger matched keyword table uses25videos. These are research-sample filters, not population attrition rates.
duration: Observed durations in six focal uploader samples. Filled points are medians; whiskers span linear25th–75thpercentiles and are not confidence intervals; open diamonds are means. All indexed videos in these six samples have known durations. The official Bashar account and Divine Insights are distinct publishers: their sampled clip/full-session mix differs. The figure does not estimate complete-channel means or compare practitioner session lengths.
matched-similarity: Matched title and caption comparisons use the same22videos in11publishers, yielding55dependent off-diagonal channel pairs. Left: raw cosines from the same pinned model, applied to different text units; their rank correlation is0.206. Right: each omission removes one publisher and all10incident pairs, leaving45pairs among10publishers. The dashed line is the full-sample correlation. The omission range[-0.043,0.379] is a descriptive influence range, not a confidence interval or a significance test.
sensitivity: Left: agreement of off-diagonal similarity rankings under specified methodological changes. Comparisons use different cohorts and interventions; these values are not model accuracy or uncertainty estimates. Right: all30English pilot caption lengths, from87to8588word tokens; median1097.5. The logarithmic horizontal axis accommodates the unequal document lengths.
